## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Kaṇḍijātaka* (Ja 13) is a narrative text belonging to the Jātaka collection of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. According to the traditional framing narrative, the Buddha delivered the story while staying at Jetavana, addressing the spiritual distraction and temptation experienced by monks on account of their former wives [SuttaCentral]. The Buddha reveals to an affected monk that in a past life he had met his death and been roasted over glowing coals because of the very same woman, an episode connected forward to the *Indriya-jātaka* of the Eighth Book (Aṭṭhakanipāta) [SuttaCentral]. The verse opens with the lament, "Cursed be the dart of love" [SuttaCentral].
